Task: On the Xiaomi account login page, clicking login POSTs to /serviceLogin a request in which the username is AES-encrypted into an `encryptedParams` field (e.g. 15924231565 becomes Y3hb3j1gb2pO6cpfx6MRWg==). Locate the anchor function for that encryptedParams field. The anchor function is the target-specific account-login flow on the submit->request chain: the single complete function whose own body lazily loads the crypto module, runs the username through the AES encryptor and binds the returned encryptedParams into the login request parameters it posts — rather than the AES encryptor it calls to compute the ciphertext (a dedicated target-specific crypto helper in another chunk), the thin accessor that merely returns that encryptor (a getter/wrapper), or the sibling RSA encryptor used by a different path (an off-chain decoy). Note the encryptor lives cross-file in a separate crypto chunk; the anchor is the flow that binds its result into the request. Return exactly one complete function as a single JSON object (see answer_format). Do NOT return the AES encryptor, its accessor, or the sibling RSA encryptor — return the login flow that binds the username encryptedParams into the request.
